back: Imprisonment without trial, used by the Rhodesian government to remove nationalist leaders.

front: What did the nationalist slogan 'one man, one vote' mean?
back: Majority rule: every adult would have an equal vote, giving power to the African majority.

front: What happened to Congress in February 1959?
back: It was banned; a state of emergency was declared and about 500 people were detained.

front: When were the NDP and ZAPU formed?
back: The NDP on 1 January 1960; ZAPU on 17 December 1961 after the NDP was banned.

front: When was ZANU formed and who led it?
back: August 1963; the Rev. Ndabaningi Sithole was president, with Robert Mugabe as secretary-general.
The armed wings of ZAPU (ZIPRA) and ZANU (ZANLA).

front: Why did the nationalist movement split in 1963?
back: Disagreement over leadership and strategy, with personal and regional rivalries; historians differ on weight.

front: How did repression push nationalists towards armed struggle?
back: Successive bans, detention of leaders and the refusal to negotiate closed peaceful politics.

front: Which states and powers supported ZAPU and ZANU?
back: ZAPU mainly the Soviet Union and its allies; ZANU mainly China; both used bases in Zambia and Tanzania.
